hints: Look closely at the location words in each option: only found in blood, can leave the blood, circulate in the blood. Do T-lymphocytes stay trapped in blood vessels?
Now check the job words: secrete cytokines, accumulate at inflammation, secrete cytotoxins, present antigens. Which jobs belong to T-cells and which belong to phagocytes that present antigens?
walkthrough:
**Where do T-lymphocytes live?**

Think of lymphocytes as patrolling cells, not prisoners in the blood. They circulate in blood and lymph, and they can squeeze out of capillaries into tissues and lymph nodes.

So any option that says they are only found in blood is already suspicious.

**What do T-lymphocytes actually do?**

Helper T-cells secrete cytokines to activate other cells, and cytotoxic T-cells kill infected body cells. Both types are attracted to chemical signals and accumulate where there is inflammation and infection.

They do not present antigens. That is the job of antigen-presenting cells like macrophages and dendritic cells.

**Pick the fully correct description**

Option B fits perfectly: they can leave the blood and gather at sites of inflammation. The other options each mix up location with only or always, or give T-cells the wrong job like presenting antigens or simply releasing cytotoxins on exposure to bacteria.

options.A: False because of the word only. T-lymphocytes are found in blood, lymph, lymph nodes and tissues, not only in blood.
options.B: Correct. T-lymphocytes circulate and can exit capillaries by extravasation, then follow chemical signals to accumulate at inflamed or infected tissue.
options.C: False. Cytotoxic T-cells kill virus-infected or abnormal body cells after specific activation, they do not simply secrete cytotoxins whenever exposed to bacteria.
options.D: False. T-lymphocytes do not present antigens. Antigen presentation is done by phagocytes such as macrophages and dendritic cells, and B-lymphocytes.
